By this common order, Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 283/2016 and 679/2016 shall be decided.

2. M.A. No. 283/2016 has been filed by the insurance company, and M.A. No. 679/2016 has been filed by the claimants against the award dated 30/11/2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior, in Claim Case No. 93/2013.

3. It is not out of place to mention here that the Claims Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company on account of violation of the insurance policy but has applied the principle of "pay and recover."

Accordingly, in M.A. No. 283 of 2016, the insurance company has challenged the direction of "pay and recover," whereas in M.A. No. 679 of 2016, the claimants have prayed for enhancement of compensation amount.

4. Challenging the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for insurance company that once the Claims Tribunal had come to a conclusion that there was a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, then it should have completely NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL: 28230 M.A. Nos. 283/2016 and 679/2016 exonerated the insurance company and should not have applied the principle of "pay and recover."
5.

sentences.text: 7. Insurance policy is a statutory contract between the insured and the insurer, and there is no privity of contract between the insurer and the claimants.
Thus, the claimants cannot be made to suffer on account of violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured.
8. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by applying the principle of "pay and recover."
9. Accordingly, M.A. No. 283/2016 is hereby dismissed.

sentences.text: It is submitted by counsel for appellants/claimants that the Claims Tribunal has taken the monthly notional income of deceased as 4,000/- but as per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the month income of deceased should have been taken as 5,270/-.
The appellants are also entitled for future prospects at the rate of 40%.
It is further submitted that the compensation awarded under other heads is also on the lower side.
11. Per contra, counsel for the insurance company has supported the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

12. Considered the submissions made by counsel for parties.
13.

It is a well-established principle of law that where the parties have failed to prove the income of the deceased, then the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act can be taken into consideration.

On the date of accident, the minimum wages of an unskilled labourer were 5,270/-,
and accordingly, the Claims Tribunal should have taken the monthly wages of the deceased as 5,270/- in place of 4,000/-.

The appeal has been valued at 1,52,000/-, and court fee of 3,800/- has already been paid.
Therefore, the appellant is liable to pay further court fee on 3,76,032/-.
Accordingly, the compensation amount is enhanced by a further sum of 5,28,032/- (Rupees Five Lakh Twenty Eight Thousand and Thirty Two only).

16. It is observed that if a further court fee of 94,000.80/- (Rupees Ninety Four Thousand and Eighty Paise only) is paid within a period of one month, then the entire amount of 5,28,032/- shall be payable to the claimants; otherwise, only a further amount of 1,52,000/- shall be payable to the claimants (because the court fee has already been paid on the said amount).
17.
The remaining conditions of the award shall remain the same.
18. Accordingly, M.A. No. 679/2016 succeeds and is hereby allowed.
